definition.requirement: Supported provider entry routes initiate the configured provider flow without authenticating the request.
Provider callbacks validate provider identity and complete with an explicit browser outcome.
OAuth state and request binding are validated and replay is rejected.
Cancellation, provider rejection, and recoverable callback failure produce explicit safe recovery outcomes.
Authenticated identities resolve through canonical OVVAULTS identity records without duplicate creation.
A session is issued only after verified canonical identity resolution.
Valid sessions persist and remain bound to their canonical identity.
A valid persisted session restores after process or browser restart while revocation remains effective.
Expired, invalid, and revoked sessions are rejected with an explicit outcome.
Logout invalidates the server session and clears client credentials.
Production authentication uses bounded canonical OVVAULTS connectivity.
The serving release declares and verifies the exact compatible authentication schema.
The release artifact and canonical ledger agree on migration identity and checksum.
Normal VVAULT login and restored sessions do not require AUTH tooling or an AUTH verifier process at runtime.
A returning canonical owner receives a session without a passkey, recovery-code, or device-approval gate.

A newly verified canonical identity enters PENDING_ENROLLMENT and activates after accepting the current required legal documents; activation rotates the pending session into a NORMAL canonical session without requiring a passkey, recovery code, or device-approval ceremony.
